'''Nicholas William Hanges''' (October 5, 1949 – July 20, 2019) was a mathematician and professor at [[Lehman College]] of the [[City University of New York]], known for his work in [[partial differential equations]] and the theory of [[several complex variables]].

==Education and career==
Hanges earned his B.S degree in mathematics from the [[New York City College]] in 1970. He received his M.A. (1975) and Ph.D. (1976) from [[Purdue University]],<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=16673|title=Nicholas Hanges}}</ref><ref name=ias/><ref>[https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/dissertations/AAI7715413/ Purdue University Dissertation Repository]</ref> under the supervision of [[M. Salah Baouendi]]. He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1977–1978, 1980–1981, 1991-1992 and again in 1994.<ref name=ias>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/nicholas-hanges|title=Nicholas Hanges at the Institute for Advanced Study|date=9 December 2019 |accessdate=August 15, 2020}}</ref> In 1983, Hanges joined the faculty of Lehman College of the City University of New York as a professor of mathematics from the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. From 2017 he served as Chairman of the Mathematics Department.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lehman.cuny.edu/lehman-today/provost/8-24-17/index.html|title=Lehman Magazine|date=July 13, 2017|accessdate=2020-08-18}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*In 1982, Hanges received an [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref name=ias/><ref name=sloan>{{cite web|url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database?page=450|title=Sloan Fellows Database|accessdate=Nov 1, 2024}}</ref>
